bullets.title: October selloff: NDX -7%, SOX -15% on AI capex/financing fears; equal-weight outperforms
bullets.body: The Nasdaq fell ~7% in October (worst since Mar-25) while the SOX dropped 15.4% — the index's third-largest single-day underperformance in 15+ years occurred Oct 30 — as the AI trade shifted from a demand debate to a financing debate mid-month. CoreWeave credit stress, Meta's 'hundreds of billions' capital needs, and Intel's catastrophic PC/guide miss drove eight consecutive session SOX losses. Equal-weight S&P outperformed cap-weight by ~590bp, with 60% of S&P constituents above their 50-day MA vs. 21% in late September. The S&P 500 ended October -0.93%.

bullets.title: Big Tech earnings: MSFT beats Azure 48%, GOOGL -12.6% on Search miss, AMZN AWS guides 40%+ for 2027-28
bullets.body: Microsoft delivered F1Q Azure at +48% (guided 49-50%), ~50% operating margins, and raised commercial RPO to $677B — described as the week's beacon. Alphabet fell 12.6% on Search growing only +12% vs. +14-15% expected, with AI Mode pressuring monetization. Amazon's AWS grew 39% (missed elevated buy-side +42-43% bogey) but management guided 40%+ growth in both 2027 and 2028, and the $578B backlog grew $82B q/q; 4Q operating income guidance midpoint missed by ~$1.5B. ServiceNow fell 28%+ on 4Q cRPO guide of 18.5% vs ~20% expected despite raising AI ACV target to $1.7B.

bullets.title: Intel crashes 25%+ on worst day since 1974: PC down 25% h/h, negative FCF in 2027
bullets.body: Intel's 4Q revenue guidance of $15-16B (vs ~$17B expected) reflected a PC unit TAM decline of ~12% in 2026 and ~10% in 2027 as memory cost inflation drove demand destruction. The Israel Fab 28 explosion added a $300M/200bp gross margin headwind in Q4 and Q1. Data Center/AI was up 78% y/y and beat, but PC (CCG) fell ~5% y/y and guided down >20% sequentially in 4Q. 2027 is expected to be a negative FCF investment year. Multiple downgrades followed: BofA to Neutral ($100 from $145), Roth to Neutral ($70 from $120), Seaport to Neutral.

bullets.title: AI financing narrative dominates: META raises $95B, AVGO backstops $63B Anthropic deal, SpaceX GPU $40B
bullets.body: The week's primary macro AI theme was financing. Meta announced ~$97.5B in equity raises (including $60B ATM starting Q1 2027) with Nvidia, AMD, and Broadcom as cornerstone investors. Broadcom arranged a $63B debt package for Anthropic chip purchases including residual value guarantees. SpaceX closed a $40B GPU deal. These moves collectively eased near-term concerns about AI capex availability. Anthropic filed its S-1 (ticker ANT, Nasdaq) showing H1'26 revenue of $16.3B (+1,400% YoY), 11,900+ enterprise customers spending $100K+, and $657B+ in future compute commitments from major CSPs.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler capex: 2026 broadly flat, but 2027 ramp required — sellside questions sustainability
bullets.body: Meta guided $135-145B CY2026 capex; Alphabet held $195-205B; Microsoft lowered slightly to ~$170B on third-party delays; Amazon held ~$220B with 'meaningfully more' in 2027. 22V Research noted the 2027 implied ramp is enormous — Microsoft has not broken $50-60B quarterly, while shareholder pressure on Amazon and Alphabet around negative FCF and AI ROI is intensifying. Piper Sandler flagged that the 2026 hyperscaler capex revision was the lowest in 3+ years, a late-cycle signal. Multiple desks flagged that only 1% of hyperscaler capex revision was the lowest in 3+ years.

bullets.title: Hedge fund de-risking at historic extremes: TMT funds -12% MTD, systematic worst week since Dec '23
bullets.body: Global hedge fund net returns fell ~3.5-4% in October. TMT-focused funds dropped 11.9-12.6% MTD, cutting YTD gains to just ~5%. GS Systematic L/S saw its worst weekly drawdown since December 2023. US Tactical Positioning Monitor fell to the 33rd percentile. Cumulative de-grossing exceeded 6% of book — more extreme than the late July/August episode and near 2018 extremes. Multi-strats were flat on the day but down ~0.9% MTD. Prior -3 sigma events in the L/S spread saw positive forward 20-day spreads in 6 of 7 cases with average rebound of +1%.

bullets.title: Systematic selling estimated at $165-220B as vol spikes; pension buying ~$46B partial offset
bullets.body: UBS estimated risk-control funds would sell $165-220B total after the vol spike, with $55-70B on Oct 30 and $110-150B the following Monday. Levered ETFs were set to sell $35B, concentrated in semiconductors ($16.8B) and QQQ ($10.1B). This was the first meaningful one-day risk-control rebalancing since November 2025. CTA medium-term trigger levels for S&P were at ~7,554 (still intact). Month-end pension rebalancing was estimated to bring ~$46B in global equity buying as partial offset.

bullets.title: Fed holds at 4%; Chair Warsh signals neutral rate 'likely higher'; December hike ~75-85% priced
bullets.body: The FOMC held the fed funds rate at 3.75-4.00% with two dissenters who preferred a 25bp hike. Chair Warsh's press conference indicated the neutral policy rate is likely higher from current levels but offered limited new information — 22V Research noted Warsh spoke more for himself than the committee, shortening the shelf life of the press conference's market impact. Q3 GDP printed at 3.4% annualized with private final domestic demand at 4.9% (strongest pace in 25 years ex-COVID). December hike probability was priced at 73-85% across desks.

bullets.title: Sticky inflation: core PCE 0.32% m/m, ECI in line but benefits surge 6.4%; Fed faces hawkish dilemma
bullets.body: September core PCE came in at 0.32% m/m with core services ex-housing at 0.37%; 52% of PCE categories are rising above 3% y/y. The Q3 ECI showed total compensation at +3.4% y/y, but the acceleration was driven by health insurance costs (+6.4% y/y) not wage gains. Multiple desks flagged that sticky inflation measures are worsening appreciably and that nominal spending growth at ~6% is too strong for inflation to return to target without a productivity surge. 22V Research maintained a neutral stance on all risk factors through year-end citing unimproving inflation and the scenario risk from AI capex collapse.

bullets.title: S&P earnings growth 30% with 82% beat rate, but magnitude of surprises below historical norms
bullets.body: Q3 blended S&P 500 EPS growth stood at 30.2% (above the 29.6% expected at quarter-end), with 82% of reported companies beating — in line with the 1-year average. However, the aggregate EPS beat was only +1.9% above expectations vs. a 13.8% 1-year average positive surprise, and revenue beats were similarly thin at +1.7% vs. +2.1% 1-year average. Jefferies noted this was the biggest downside T+1 earnings day move for Tech in their 12-year dataset. The message across multiple desks: beats barely rewarded as drama has shifted to outlooks, not crystalized reality.

bullets.title: Value/equal-weight breakout vs. growth; tech seasonally strongest Nov-Jan but software outperforms semis technically
bullets.body: The Russell 1000 Value/Growth ratio broke above two-year resistance. SPX averaged a 2.4% November gain since 1950, finishing higher 73% of years when entering the month above the 200-day MA. Tech ranked highest for momentum despite AI-related weakness; software shows stronger technicals than semis. Post-midterm seasonal patterns are historically strong: S&P 500 has been higher 12 months after every midterm since 1950 (19/19), averaging ~15%, and Nasdaq positive all 13 post-midterm windows since 1974. Sector momentum: Tech +11%, Financials +6% lead; Consumer Discretionary -11%, Utilities -5% lag.

bullets.title: 10Y Treasuries rally to 4.91-4.93% from 5.36% highs as AI/growth fears overtake inflation
bullets.body: The 10-year Treasury yield fell ~35bp in October as AI/growth concerns overtook inflation worries. JPM technical strategy noted the 10-year rally stalling at 4.93-5.02% resistance with potential extension to 4.75-4.80% if equity selling intensifies. 22V Research's John noted the 30-year broke bearish trend thresholds and was considering covering TLT shorts. The yield decline was occurring simultaneously with WTI rallying 15.2% to above $100 on US-Iran escalation risk — a concerning combination per multiple macro strategists who noted rates below 5% with oil at $100 is a negative signal.

bullets.title: Midterm elections: Democrats favored for House (91%) and Senate (67%); data center backlash a swing factor
bullets.body: Prediction markets showed Democrats at 66% for a sweep, with 56% of Americans reporting giving considerable thought to the midterms — the highest on record. Democrats held a 10-point enthusiasm advantage (58% vs 48%). Voter proximity to data centers is shifting preferences toward Democrats (+7pp among those within 2km); among Trump 2024 voters near data centers, 17% intend to vote Democratic vs. 6% of those farther away. The Texas race remained close (Abbott +2-4%), significant because Texas hosts 35%+ of AI factory buildouts. California Prop 40 (billionaire tax) polls at only 25% support.

bullets.title: Memory cycle: SK Hynix blowout (7x profit, HBM sold out to 2029); NAND showing moderation with Kioxia guidance miss
bullets.body: SK Hynix reported a 7x quarterly profit surge, launched a ¥100T ($75B) shareholder return program, and confirmed HBM/DRAM demand exceeds supply through 2030. Long-term agreements cover >50% of 2027-2028 production. In contrast, Kioxia's December quarter guidance missed by 14-16% on slower ASP growth (3-4% QoQ vs. ~30% prior) and smartphone softening. SanDisk beat strongly with data center at ~50% of industry bit demand; its NBM pipeline now covers 50% of FY27 bits and 67% of FY28 bits, extending beyond 2030. Memory's divergence — HBM/DRAM tight, NAND normalizing — is a key AI infrastructure read-through.

bullets.title: Binance $6.3B hack — largest crypto exchange breach on record — hits COIN, HOOD sentiment
bullets.body: A compromised device at Binance resulted in $6.3B in unauthorized withdrawals — the largest crypto exchange breach on record. ~$3B was frozen on-chain with help from Tether, Circle, and Ripple. Bitcoin fell 4.6% to $76.7K. Morgan Stanley expects downside risk to Coinbase/Gemini 2027 earnings and valuation multiples. Crypto miners (BTBT, RIOT, MARA) fell 9-12%. HOOD fell 13.5% on both the earnings miss and crypto contagion. KeyBanc noted share gain opportunity for Coinbase from international but offering gaps may limit relevance. The incident reflects custody and operational failures, not blockchain flaws.

bullets.title: Oil surges 15% in October to above $100/bbl on Iran escalation; Hormuz flows drop 27% from peak
bullets.body: WTI rallied 15.2% to above $100, marking the fourth consecutive monthly gain, driven by US-Iran escalation risks. Crude and product flows exiting the Gulf of Oman fell to 12.5Mb/d from an early-October peak of 17.2Mb/d — a 27% decline tracked by UBS Evidence Lab via AIS data. Multiple desks flagged that oil at $100+ with 10-year yields below 5% is a stagflationary warning signal. Brent crude was cited as a Hedgeye top long with a target of ~$119-122. 22V Research maintained oil bull thesis with a gold expensive relative to oil at 38x vs. the 20x long-term average.

bullets.title: DoorDash acquires Instacart for ~$17B; MRVL in advanced talks to acquire Lumentum
bullets.body: DoorDash confirmed acquisition of Instacart at ~$65/share (~$17B equity value), deal expected to close end-2027/1H2028. Citi modeled $500M+ annual synergies, accelerating DoorDash's grocery/retail vertical by years. JPMorgan suspended ratings on both due to acting as financial advisor to DASH. Separately, Marvell was reported to be in advanced talks to acquire Lumentum in what could be one of the largest tech deals ever (LITE market cap ~$83B); deal expected to be all-stock at a modest premium. Wolfe noted the deal's strategic rationale (vertical optics integration) but flagged peak-cycle valuation and MRVL customer neutrality risks.

bullets.title: Reddit -36% weekly on Google Search referral collapse; logged-in transition creates near-term DAU air pocket
bullets.body: Reddit reported 3Q revenue beating (+54% ad growth, 54% incremental margins) but disclosed a ~1M/week decline in Google Search referrals in October, risking low-double-digit total DAU decline in 4Q. The stock fell 36% on the week. Raymond James maintained Strong Buy at $150, arguing the pivot to app-only/logged-in users (who drive >80% of monetization and are 5x more engaged) is structurally positive. Citi cut PT to $186 from $245 on near-term execution risk but maintained Buy. The Google AI Mode monetization headwind affecting Reddit is part of a broader Search disruption theme.

bullets.title: Anthropic IPO filed (ticker ANT, Nasdaq): 1,400% revenue growth, $855B compute commitments, $1.5T valuation target
bullets.body: Anthropic's S-1 revealed H1'26 revenue of $16.3B (+1,400% YoY), narrowed operating loss to $693M from $2.1B, and disclosed adjusted net income of $2.7B vs. a $1.7B loss year-ago. The customer base grew from 950 to 11,900 with $100K+ TTM spend in one year. Compute commitments total $657B+, including Amazon ($110B through 2036), Google ($114.5B+), Broadcom ($161.2B), and SpaceX.AI ($120.5B). IPO valuation targets ~$1.5T with timing estimated around November 20. 22V Research noted the company needs ~$200B+ ARR exiting 2027 to cover compute commitments — describing the IPO as the last major AI catalyst through year-end.
